_provenance: Captured from a real tenant on 2026-10-15 through pm-ai's own Graph client: the first page of GET /teams/{team}/channels/{channel}/messages?$top=50&$expand=replies (the URL GraphClient.channel_messages builds) for one listed channel. Redacted before it left the machine. Ids come from HMAC-SHA256 under a random 32-byte key that was never written down, so the mapping cannot be reproduced, or confirmed by hashing a guessed real value: GUIDs come out v4-shaped, Teams ids keep their shape (`19:...@thread.tacv2`, `19:meeting_...@thread.v2`, `..._...@unq.gbl.spaces`), and online-meeting and other opaque ids keep their length and alphabet. People are mapped per user id: one id is one 'Person N' across the channel and chat fixtures, and `mentionText` and the text inside `<at>` carry the same label. Free text: every word is replaced by lowercase letters of random length (2 to 9) in its own script, digits become 0, and punctuation, spacing and HTML entities are kept. Kept as recorded: keys, value types, timestamps (the real instants), Graph enumerations (keys ending in Type or Status, `@odata.type`, `contentType`, `messageType` and the like), the JSON keys inside card attachments, HTML tag names and structural attributes. `href` and `src` become https://example.invalid/<token>; URL fields become https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/redacted/<token>, keeping `?$skiptoken=` where the original had one. Trimmed: the page held 49 threads (about 800 KB); 17 are kept, each whole and in the order Microsoft sent them, chosen to keep every shape on the page: HTML bodies with mentions, code, lists, links, images, emoji, strike-through and entities; an attachment-only body; reference, adaptive-card, announcement-banner and meetingReference attachments; subjects; edited messages; threads with inline replies; system events (members added, members deleted, and call events inside a thread). Thread 1129054146902, a meeting thread, is kept whole: 200 inline replies (187 of them system events) and a `replies@odata.nextLink`. The dropped threads repeat the kept shapes. No field value was edited, so `@odata.count` still says 49 and `@odata.nextLink` is the page's own. Observed on the full page: threads are in order of the root's createdDateTime, newest first. They are not in order of the latest reply: thread 1129054146902, created 2026-08-17 with replies up to 2026-10-15, sits 33rd of 49. They are not in order of the root's lastModifiedDateTime either: that thread's root reads 2026-10-15, and two other pairs of roots on the full page (neither kept) also break that order. Replies arrive newest first in every thread holding more than one. Every system event is typed `unknownFutureValue`, with the body `<systemEventMessage/>` and an `eventDetail`.
